title: High quality DNA from Fusarium oxysporum conidia for PacBio sequencing
author: Sukhwinder Kaur
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.i8ichue
materials: Sterilize all dry supplies by autoclaving.

Air dry the pellet for 15 to 20 min until there is no visible ethanol residue. Add 100 ul of EB (10mM Tris pH 8.5, Qiagen). Incubate at RT overnight. Next morning, incubate at 28 C on a platform orbit shaker at 150 rpm for 1 h.

steps.title: Prepare conidial plates
steps.instruction: Spread a Fusarium oxysporum conidial suspension onto 10–20 100‑mm Petri dishes containing potato dextrose agar to obtain ~0.5 ml packed conidial volume (~250 mg lyophilized conidia). Incubate under fluorescent lights at ~25 °C for 6–7 days.

steps.title: Harvest conidia
steps.instruction: From each plate add 5 ml sterile water, gently rub the culture with a metal “hockey stick” and collect the suspension; repeat with an additional 5 ml water and combine the washes.

steps.title: Filter conidial suspension
steps.instruction: Pour the combined suspension through two layers of Miracloth into 50 ml centrifuge tubes.

steps.title: Pellet and lyophilize conidia
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 4 °C, 3620 g for 15 min. Discard supernatant, resuspend pellet in 3–5 ml water and repeat centrifugation at 3620 g for 15 min. Remove water, freeze the pellet at –70 °C overnight, then lyophilize to dryness. Store lyophilized conidia at –70 °C until use.

steps.title: Prepare extraction buffer with RNase A
steps.instruction: For each 50 mg lyophilized conidia use 1 ml freshly prepared extraction buffer. To make 5 ml buffer combine 4 ml Milli‑Q nuclease‑free water, 1 ml 5×RNB, 240 mg PAS (sodium 4‑aminosalicylate dihydrate) and 40 mg TIPS (triisopropylnaphthalenesulfonic acid sodium); vortex until dissolved and foam disappears. Add 5 µl (50 µg) RNase A (10 mg ml⁻¹ stock). Prepare buffer immediately before extraction.

steps.title: Cool mortar and sand
steps.instruction: Cool a 9 cm‑diameter mortar with liquid N₂. Add sand, then add additional liquid N₂ to keep the sand cold.

steps.title: Grind lyophilized conidia
steps.instruction: Transfer lyophilized conidia into the cooled mortar with sand and grind vigorously for 15–20 seconds. Add more liquid N₂ as needed to maintain a cold temperature.

steps.title: Transfer ground material to extraction tube
steps.instruction: Transfer the ground conidia‑sand mixture to a 2 ml microfuge tube (T#1) containing 1 ml extraction buffer with RNase A (from step 5). Label three additional tubes (T#2, T#3, T#4) for subsequent steps; each tube will receive ~50 mg lyophilized conidia.

steps.title: Initial vortex
steps.instruction: Vortex T#1 on a horizontal low‑speed vortex mixer (~200 rpm) for 2 minutes.

steps.title: Room‑temperature incubation
steps.instruction: Incubate T#1 at room temperature for 30 minutes, inverting the tube every 5 minutes.

steps.title: Add proteinase K
steps.instruction: Add 6 µl (120 µg) proteinase K to T#1 and vortex on the low‑speed mixer for 20 minutes at room temperature.

steps.title: Ice incubation
steps.instruction: Place the tubes on ice for 5 minutes.

steps.title: First phenol‑chloroform extraction
steps.instruction: Add an equal volume of ice‑cold, buffered P:C:I (25:24:1) to T#1, vortex 15 seconds, then transfer the aqueous supernatant to a new 2 ml tube (T#2) without disturbing the interphase.

steps.title: Second phenol‑chloroform extraction
steps.instruction: Add an equal volume of ice‑cold, buffered P:C:I to T#2, vortex on a horizontal mixer for 2 minutes at 4 °C, centrifuge 15000 g for 10 minutes at 4 °C, and transfer the supernatant (800–900 µl) to a new tube (T#3).

steps.title: Chloroform‑isoamyl extraction
steps.instruction: Add an equal volume of ice‑cold chloroform:isoamyl alcohol (24:1) to T#3, vortex 15 seconds at 4 °C, centrifuge 15000 g for 5 minutes at 4 °C, then carefully transfer the supernatant to tube T#4 without disturbing the interface.

steps.title: Precipitation setup
steps.instruction: To T#4 add 0.1 volume ice‑cold 4 M NaCl and invert several times (DNA strings become visible); then add 1 volume ice‑cold isopropyl alcohol and invert gently at least 20 times.

steps.title: DNA precipitation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 10000 g for 30 minutes at 4 °C, then centrifuge the pellet again at 15000 g for 6 minutes at 4 °C. Incubate the tube on ice for 10 minutes.

steps.title: Ethanol wash
steps.instruction: Discard the supernatant, wash the pellet with 1.5 ml ice‑cold 70 % ethanol, centrifuge 13000 g for 5 minutes at room temperature. Discard supernatant, centrifuge 13000 g for 1 minute at room temperature, and remove residual ethanol with a fine‑tip pipettor (P10 or P20).

steps.title: Initial DNA quantification
steps.instruction: Measure DNA concentration with a Nanodrop and Qubit. Acceptable Nanodrop ratios: 260/280 = 1.8–1.9, 260/230 > 2. Qubit should read ≥200 ng µl⁻¹ (often ~0.1 ng µl⁻¹ before cleanup).

steps.title: AMPure bead addition
steps.instruction: Bring AMPure beads to room temperature, gently pipet them, and add 0.45× (or 0.5×) volume of beads to the DNA solution. Flick the tube to mix thoroughly (do not vortex).

steps.title: Collect beads briefly
steps.instruction: Spin the tubes at 7000 g for 2–3 seconds to collect the beads at the tube bottom.

steps.title: DNA binding to beads
steps.instruction: Shake the tubes at 200 rpm on a horizontal vortex mixer for 10 minutes, then incubate on a rotating wheel at 22 rpm for 20 minutes.

steps.title: Bead pelleting and magnetic capture
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 7000 g for 10 seconds to pellet the beads, then place the tubes in a magnetic rack to immobilize the beads on the side of the tube.

steps.title: Remove supernatant
steps.instruction: Carefully pipette off the supernatant (save as a backup) without disturbing the bead pellet.

steps.title: Ethanol washes of beads
steps.instruction: With the tubes on the magnetic rack, add 70 % ethanol to the rim of each tube, avoiding the pellet; pipette off the ethanol, then repeat a second 70 % ethanol wash. Remove all ethanol without disturbing the beads.

steps.title: Remove residual ethanol
steps.instruction: Take the tubes off the magnetic rack, centrifuge at 7000 g for 30 seconds to collect residual ethanol, then remove ethanol with a fine‑tip pipettor (P20 or P10). Verify no ethanol droplets remain; repeat the ethanol wash if necessary.

steps.title: Elute DNA from beads
steps.instruction: Add elution buffer (EB) volume sufficient to achieve >100 ng µl⁻¹ DNA (typically 50–100 µl). Flick to mix until homogeneous, centrifuge 7000 g for 30 seconds, place tubes back on the magnetic rack for 5–10 minutes, then transfer the cleared DNA solution to a clean 1.5 ml microfuge tube, avoiding any beads.

steps.title: Final DNA quality check
steps.instruction: Quantify DNA again with Nanodrop and Qubit. Acceptable Nanodrop ratios: 260/280 = 1.7–1.9, 260/230 > 2.0, and Qubit/Nanodrop concentration ratio > 0.7.
